title: Favourable-move confirmation before entry: no confirmation vs $10 vs $15 vs $20 on the frozen engine's signals (and on structure and random triggers): TP-first, SL-first and net expectancy after costs, in and out of sample
status: APPROVED by the operator 2026-11-15 (directive quoted below); written and committed before any of its code; research only, no production change
approval: Operator, 2026-11-15 (chat), UPDATE TO THE MASTER TRADING DIRECTIVE, section 2: "Investigate whether $10, $15 and $20 confirmation thresholds improve actual TP-first outcomes. Backtest each threshold independently and compare against: No movement confirmation. $10 confirmation. $15 confirmation. $20 confirmation. ... Use historical replay and out-of-sample testing. Do not assume that the largest confirmation is automatically the best. If price moves $20 but the remaining distance to the target is too small, or the stop-loss becomes disproportionately large, reject the trade. Recalculate entry, SL, TP and risk/reward after confirmation." Section 4: "Where both TP and SL occur within the same candle and intrabar ordering cannot be established, classify the result as ambiguous rather than assuming TP was reached first. Do not manipulate stop-loss or target distances merely to improve historical win rates." Section 6: "Recommend the best-performing threshold only if the evidence supports it out of sample."
unsealed_data_also_used: recent: 2026-01-01 to the end of the research history, scored after a 59-day warm-up inside it (B19 'recent'); reported, not decisive
prior_evidence_disclosed_before_running: B19 (2026-11-07) tested $15 / $20 close confirmation on the same engine triggers: development ENG $15 +$2.67/oz on 20 trades (INSUFFICIENT); validation, opened once, -$3.04/oz on 49 trades (the edge reversed). The validation and holdout partitions have therefore already been read for $15 / $20 confirmation: B30's out-of-sample test there is NOT a first look. The $10 level, the two-target plan and the per-trigger accounting are new.

B21: liquidity / breakout alerts with confirmation: FAIL 8 of 8. B25: no execution-timing variant kept the confirmed odds. B24-CONFIRM-FWD ($15-$20 capped confirmation, forward): OFF by operator instruction; B30 does not change it.

The research engine runs without volume, macro or cross-asset inputs (b10.make_market, no 2020-24 volume): B19 found 64 ENG ideas on development after the REPEAT rule, so ENG samples are small; see power_stated_in_advance.
unchanged: Production alerts, the engine, config.py, the frozen website holdout (freeze key 5e4630924d663fc5:a6f2be58c74887ed), B9-GRAB-FWD, B15-ENGINE-FWD, B24 (OFF) and every other registration. B30 is research code (quantum/research/b30.py), never imported by production.
data: Twelve Data XAU/USD 15min and 1h from the research-data branch (2020-01-24 on); the SHA-256 of each partition's bars is recorded with the results. Distances are $ at $4,000 scaled by P0 / 4000 (the B19 convention, so $10 means the same relative move in 2020 as now); costs are $ per oz, unscaled.

populations.ENG (primary): the frozen engine's SIGNAL events (treatment arm, production code) on 15m, 30m, 1h and 4h, pooled with the live REPEAT rule (b19.dedupe: a trigger in the same direction within 4 h and $15 scaled of a kept one is dropped): one per idea
populations.STR (secondary): B19's structure triggers (BOS / MSS / CHoCH with the engine's bias, VWAP side and session quality >= 30 agreeing), REPEAT rule as ENG
populations.RND (null, secondary): every 8th 15m close in the scored span, both directions (B19 / B21 N2): whether a $X favourable move by itself predicts continuation, with a large sample

lifecycle_recorded_per_trigger: SETUP (trigger) -> REFERENCE (P0 = the trigger bar's close, fixed) -> REACHED_10 / REACHED_15 / REACHED_20 (first 15m high / low X beyond P0: a TOUCH, recorded, never an entry) -> CONFIRMED (the first 15m CLOSE X beyond P0) -> ELIGIBLE (confirmed and the plan checks passed) -> ACTIVE (entry at that close) | INVALIDATED | EXPIRED | REJECTED

models.Baseline: no confirmation: entry at P0 at the trigger close (the phone's entry today)

confirmation: For A / B / C: the first 15m close at least X (scaled) beyond P0 in the trigger's direction within 96 15m bars (24 h) of the trigger close. INVALIDATED first if price trades $13 (scaled) against P0 (15m high / low) or the frozen engine publishes an opposite BOS / MSS / CHoCH; a bar that both invalidates and closes beyond counts as invalidated (B19). No confirmation in 96 bars = EXPIRED. 'Valid market structure' = no opposite structure break before the confirmation. A touch of +X is not an entry.

plans.G1 (primary): the operator's plan, recal: entry E = the confirming close (Baseline: P0); stop E - 13; TP1 E + 13 for half; TP2 E + 20 for the other half; stop moved to E after TP1 (all scaled). Every executed trade risks the same $ (0.46 lot at $4,000 for $650 incl. cost, N1), so R and $ are comparable across models.
plans.G2 (secondary): levels fixed at the trig: the engine's own stop and TP1 from the SIGNAL bar (ENG only); entry at the confirming close; EXECUTE only if (TP1 - E) / (E - stop) >= 1.0 after costs, the stop is 5 to 40 (scaled) from E and the cost <= 15% of it (B19's constants, not re-chosen); otherwise REJECTED ('remaining reward too small or stop too large'). One target.
plans.G0 (arithmetic, reported, not simulated): the phone plan anchored at the trigger (stop P0 - 13, TP1 P0 + 13): after a $10 confirmation at most $3 of reward remains for at least $23 of risk (0.13 : 1); at $15 / $20 TP1 is already passed. Always REJECTED.

exits: 15m bars from the bar after the entry (Baseline: from the first bar after the trigger close), at most 192 bars (48 h), then exit at that close (TIMEOUT). A bar opening beyond a level fills at its open. Before TP1, a bar touching both the stop and TP1 = AMBIGUOUS: reported as its own outcome; in expectancy scored as the stop (never as TP). After TP1, a bar touching both TP2 and the moved stop = AMBIGUOUS-2, scored at the moved stop. Cost: the harness model cost at the entry bar (spread + 2 x slippage + commission, about $0.77-0.97/oz) primary; the operator's $0.26/oz secondary.
metrics: per population x model x plan x partition: triggers; confirmed; executed; missed (EXPIRED / INVALIDATED / REJECTED separately) and missed winners (missed triggers whose Baseline trade reached TP1 first); TP1-first %, TP2-first % (TP1 then TP2), SL-first %, AMBIGUOUS %, TIMEOUT %, each with a Wilson 95% interval; net expectancy per executed trade in R (net $ / (stop + cost)) and in $ at the $650 budget (R x 650) with a t 95% interval and a day-clustered bootstrap 95% interval (2,000 resamples, seed 30); per-trigger expectancy (a trigger not executed = 0 R); entry delay (minutes from the trigger close, mean / median); MAE and MFE ($ at $4,000 from the entry while the position is open, mean / median); reversal frequency (share of executed trades stopped first after an MFE of at least 6.5, half of TP1); realised reward-to-risk (mean net $ of winners / |mean net $ of losers|); maximum drawdown ($ at $650 per trade, cumulative in entry order) and the longest losing streak; sample size

primary_test.sample: out of sample = validation + holdout pooled (the sealed partitions)
primary_test.rule: a threshold X in {A, B, C} is SUPPORTED only if all three hold: (1) its mean R per executed trade out of sample is above 0 with the day-clustered bootstrap 95% lower bound above 0; (2) it exceeds the Baseline's out-of-sample mean R with a one-sided Welch p below 0.05 after Holm over the three thresholds; (3) the difference to the Baseline has the same sign on development. If more than one is supported, the recommendation is the one with the higher DEVELOPMENT mean R (chosen in sample, confirmed out of sample). If none is supported: no threshold is recommended on evidence.

power_stated_in_advance: ENG: B19 found 64 ideas on development and about 20 confirmed $15 trades; validation + holdout should give a similar order. With about 40 executed trades per arm and a per-trade sd near 1 R, the smallest difference detectable at 80% power (one-sided 5%) is about 0.55 R, i.e. large; a smaller real effect will most likely read INSUFFICIENT. RND has thousands of triggers and can detect about 0.05 R: it says whether a $X move by itself carries information, not whether the engine's signals do.
secondary_reported_not_decisive: STR and RND populations; G2; the operator's cost; per timeframe; 'recent' (2026); regime breakdown (trending / ranging / volatile / news window, B19 regimes); TP1-first rate against the break-even rate at that cost
not_done_by_design: No stop or target distance is searched or tuned here (operator section 4; AUDIT_PROMPT section 9). Stop / target grids were explored in B19 (S10 / S13 / SATR / SSTR x 15-30), B27 and B29 and are cited, not re-run.
trials_log: each population x model x plan x partition x cost evaluated is appended to research/trials.jsonl (harness.log_trial)
decision: SUPPORTED: the report recommends that threshold for the alerts' confirmation rule and states its out-of-sample interval; it still does not make the signals a validated edge unless (1) holds, and the forward record decides. NOT SUPPORTED: the report says so; the operator's confirmation rule can still run in the alerts as a stated risk preference (C1), labelled as not shown to raise TP-first odds; NO TRADE remains the verdict for a signal without validated edge.
